IC1: Present [AND] to ED [AND] primary for management of LBP, defined as pain originating between the lower border of the scapulae and the upper gluteal folds. [NOT] Flank pain, that is pain originating from tissues lateral to the paraspinal muscles, will not be included.
IC2: Musculoskeletal etiology of low back. Patients with [NOT] [NOT] non-musculoskeletal etiologies such as urinary tract infection [OR], ovarian cysts [OR], or influenza like illness will be excluded. The primary clinical diagnosis, at the conclusion of the ED visit, must be a diagnosis consistent with non-traumatic, non-radicular, musculoskeletal LBP.
IC3: Patient is to be discharged home. Patients admitted to the hospital are more likely to be treated with parenteral medication and therefore are not appropriate for this study.
IC4: Age 18-64 Enrollment will be limited to adults younger than 65 years because of the increased risk of adverse [AND] medication effects in the elderly.
IC5: [NOT] Non-radicular pain. Patients will be [NOT] excluded if the pain radiates below the gluteal folds in a radicular pattern.
IC6: Pain duration <2 weeks [OR] (336 hours). Patients with more than two weeks of pain are at increased risk of poor pain and functional outcomes.(9)
IC7: Prior to the acute attack of LBP, back pain [NOT] cannot occur more frequently than once per month. Patients with more frequent back pain are at increased risk of poor pain and functional outcomes.(9)
IC8: Non-traumatic LBP: no substantial [OR] and direct trauma to the back within the previous month
IC9: Functionally impairing back pain: A baseline score of > 5 on the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire
